fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Walkway; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Circular Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install reflective address markers at both driveway entrances so responders can identify the correct entry point from the road.
• Mark which driveway entrance is preferred for emergency vehicles to avoid confusion during an incident.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the circular driveway so overhead and side clearance is maintained for fire apparatus and large emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the perimeter fencing to keep fence line gates and openings visible and reachable by responders.
• Keep any gates in the perimeter fence unlocked or equipped with a Knox-Box or combination lock so responders can reach the rear of the property without delay.
• Post a simple property map at the primary driveway entrance showing the location of the house, alternate access points, and any rear areas that are difficult to reach.
• Clear a path along at least one side of the residence to give responders a walking route from the front driveway to the rear yard.
• Keep the walkway to the main entrance free of planters, landscaping features, or other objects that could slow responder movement.
• Confirm the circular driveway surface can support the weight of a fire engine and that no decorative edging or landscaping extends into the travel path.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Green Space; Grass Cover; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Along Driveway; Multiple Access Routes; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the scattered clusters closest to the structure to reduce the amount of vegetation that could carry fire toward the building.
• Trim or remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately next to the structure.
• Cut grass near the structure and around outbuildings short, especially during dry periods.
• Clear overhanging branches and shrubs along the driveway to keep the travel lane fully open for vehicles.
• Separate shrubs from the base of the structure by removing those within a few feet of the foundation or walls.
• Remove dead or dry grass and plant material from the open green space areas closest to the structure.
• Thin scattered shrubs between tree clusters and the structure to reduce the amount of connected vegetation between them.
• Keep the area under tree clusters near the structure clear of low-hanging branches and accumulated dead material on the ground.
• Maintain the existing separation between vegetation and the structure by trimming back any plants that are beginning to close that gap.
